doc.title: Rossano Sportiello interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 2, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Thinking ahead, monologue versus conversation, and empathy
summary: Improvising resembles conversation; solo piano is a monologue and band playing needs musical and personal compatibility.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: You had said some time ago about being in the moment. But also in describing the way you were composing on the fly, you almost have to be thinking a little bit about what you just played and how long am I going to play this thing. So you’re in the moment but you’re —

Yeah. It’s the same thing that you do in the conversation, talking. Again. Because while I’m talking I have to keep in mind what I just said. Because I have to keep the idea flowing and then I have to look a little bit ahead because I know in which direction I want to go with — by expressing my concept. I want to follow that direction. Or at a certain point I need to drop this subject and introduce another subject, and then develop that © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
subject in my conversation. And it’s the same thing in the playing of the music. Now if you’re playing a solo piano concert I say it’s like to make a monologue. A monologue? You say in English?

Right. Monologo we say in Italian. While if you’re playing with a band of musicians then it’s really like a conversation. Like you are listening to each other and reacting to each other in different ways you know.
And the group interaction like that works better with certain combinations of people?

Yes. Absolutely. Because you have to be with people that have got a certain common feeling about the music, that see the music in a kind of similar way. And there is musical and personal — how do you say — compatibility?

Yes. That’s very important. So in other words if you like very much the way your colleague sounds and you like him or her very much personally, and there is an understanding, that’s the most beautiful feeling.
How would you say that in Italian?
Oh. La cosa più bella. The most beautiful thing.
